transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, thank you for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up an appointment from someone who needs it more, I know how busy clinics get... but, um, I guess I'm here because my body just feels, like, completely drained? 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but lately, even just walking from my car to the clinic today, or... or being at work and just trying to open the EHR... it just feels like it takes everything I have. Is it okay that I came in for that? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out.
How long have you been feeling this way, with your energy being so low and everyday tasks feeling draining?

Um, well... I guess it's been a while. I really should have come in sooner, I'm sorry. I just kept thinking I could push through it, you know? But... I'd say it's been about nine months. 

I had this time right before this where I had, like, a really high-energy period, and I was getting so much done at work and just feeling great. But then I just kind of... crashed. And ever since that crash, for the last nine months, I've just been stuck feeling so exhausted and, um, depressed. And just really guilty about not being able to do my job right or keep up with things. 

I feel bad even complaining about it, but... I hope I'm explaining this okay. Does that make sense, to crash for that long?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still... I still like the things I used to like. I don't want you to think I've just given up on everything or, you know, become totally checked out. I still try to do things. 

It's just that, um, with how tired I am, I guess I don't always have the energy to do them as much? But the interest is definitely still there. Like, I still want to hang out with my friends, and I still care about my job at the hospital, I really do. I just... I might stay home a little more often right now because I don't want to bring everybody down if I'm too tired to be fun. 

But I haven't lost interest, I promise. Is it okay that I'm just too tired to do them sometimes? I'm really trying my best to keep up.
Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was unusually elevated, you felt extremely energetic, or you didn't need much sleep for several days at a time?

Um, well... yeah, I guess so. Like I mentioned before, I did have that time right before the crash where I had a ton of energy. And mostly it was really good! Some days I just felt, like, absolutely amazing and completely unstoppable. I was getting so much done. 

But, um... I feel really bad admitting this, because I really try to be a good team player at work... but during that time, if one of the nurses corrected my documentation, or... or if they told me to just slow down a little, I would kind of... snap at them? 

I don't know why I did that. It just felt like they were insulting me, you know? I really didn't mean to be rude, and I tried not to make a big deal out of it. I hope you don't think I'm a difficult person to work with. Is it normal to get a little irritable like that when you're just really focused and energetic?

How long did that high-energy period last before you 'crashed'? And during that time, did you also experience things like sleeping much less than usual, thoughts racing through your head, or doing things that had some risk or consequence, like spending sprees or impulsive decisions?

Um, well... let's see. The whole... I guess you could call it a crisis, or just that really intense period... it built up over about two months. It started right after the clinic where I work changed my responsibilities. I wanted to show them I could handle it, you know? So I was just really throwing myself into it. 

As for the other stuff... um, I guess I was sleeping a little less? But I really didn't feel like I needed it, I just felt so productive. And my thoughts were definitely moving pretty fast, but I thought that was just because I had so many good ideas for work. 

I didn't do anything too crazy, I promise. I mean, I might have spent a little more money than usual, just buying some new scrubs and stuff for the job, but... nothing bad. I was just trying to do my best at work. Does that sound like a normal reaction to getting new responsibilities? I just really wanted to impress my supervisors.
Have you ever had another period in your life where you felt unusually energetic, elevated, or irritable for several days or more, where it was a noticeable change from your usual self?

Um, no, I... I don't think so. I really try to keep things pretty steady, you know? I mean, I'm only eighteen, so I haven't been working at the clinic that long, but I've always tried to just be a good, reliable employee. 

I don't remember any other time where I felt like that, with all that energy and... and the snapping at people. That really isn't like me at all, I swear. I usually get along with everyone. 

So, yeah, I'm pretty sure this was the only time. I mean, everyone has good days and bad days, right? But nothing like what just happened. Is it okay if it just happened this once? I'm really hoping it was just the stress of the new responsibilities and not something... something wrong with me.

Have you ever had any other times in your life, even before you started working at the clinic, where you felt unusually energetic, unusually confident, or were getting more done than usual — even for just a few days — that was different from your usual self?

Um, no... I really don't think so. Even back in high school, I was always just... pretty normal, I think. I tried to be a good student, turn my assignments in on time, not cause any trouble for my teachers. 

I don't remember ever feeling super confident or having crazy energy like that before. I mean, maybe I'd get a little excited before a big test if I studied hard, but... that's just normal teenager stuff, right? Everyone feels good when they're prepared. 

I've always just tried to be steady and do what's expected of me. I really don't want you to think I have a history of acting out or being erratic. I'm usually very level-headed, I promise. Does that make sense? I just... I really think this recent thing was a one-time reaction to the clinic.
Have you ever had any other times in your life when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless for several days or more — even before this recent nine-month period?

Um... well, before this recent time? No, I don't think so. I've always tried to stay pretty positive, you know? Just keep my head down and do my work. 

But... um... since that really intense period ended, the one we were just talking about... I guess I have been feeling pretty down. Like, really down. After all that energy just sort of... disappeared, I started feeling really empty most days. Just kind of hopeless. 

I kept thinking that I had already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started, because of how I acted at the clinic. It's just been really hard to shake that feeling. But I'm trying my best to stay professional, I promise. I don't want to be a burden or anything. Is it normal to feel that way after being so stressed out? I just want to make sure I'm reacting the right way to all of this.

Have you ever had a period where you felt an unusually strong need to keep doing things, maybe even pushing yourself beyond what was reasonable, even if it meant not sleeping much or feeling like you couldn’t slow down?

Um... well... I guess during that time we were just talking about, I did stay really, really busy. But I was just trying to be a hard worker, you know? 

I just... I had so much energy that I couldn't really sit still at all. So I put it to good use! I kept walking the halls, checking on all the rooms, and I reorganized all the medical supplies so they'd be perfectly neat and easier for the nurses to find. I just kept looking for more things to do to help out... even, um... even after my shift was technically over. 

I probably shouldn't have stayed late like that without being asked, but I just couldn't seem to slow down, and I wanted to make sure everything was perfect for the next shift. I was just trying to go above and beyond for the team. That's a good thing for an employee to do, right? I really hope they didn't think I was being weird or in the way by staying past my hours... I just wanted to show them I was dedicated.
During that high-energy period, did you ever feel so unusually powerful, important, or unstoppable—like you had special abilities or were on a unique mission?

Um... well... I wouldn't say "powerful" or "unstoppable," exactly. That sounds a little... extreme, maybe? I was just really passionate about my job. 

But, um... I guess I did feel like... like I was seeing things really clearly. Maybe clearer than anyone else. I started thinking that I actually understood patient care better than the nurses, or even the clinic managers. Which sounds terrible to say out loud, I know! I wasn't trying to be arrogant, I promise. 

It's just... I really believed that if they would just listen to my ideas, I could change the whole system and make everything run perfectly. I thought I had figured out the best way to do things, and I just wanted to help them see it. That's just showing initiative, right? I mean, it's good to care about improving the workplace, isn't it? I really hope I didn't come across as disrespectful to the staff... I just wanted to be as helpful as possible.

Did you notice a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like being unusually irritable or extremely confident—even for a few days, where others might have noticed you were acting out of the ordinary?

Um... well... I guess my mood was a little bit all over the place, if I'm being completely honest. I mean, mostly I just felt... amazing. Like, really, really good and capable, like I could handle anything they threw at me. 

But... um... there were a few times where I guess I wasn't as polite as I should have been. Like, if one of the nurses corrected my documentation, or... or if they told me I needed to slow down and stop doing so much. I... I kind of snapped at them. 

I feel really bad about it now. At the time, it just felt like they were insulting me, or telling me I wasn't doing a good job when I was trying so hard. I know I shouldn't have reacted that way. It's not professional to get irritable with your coworkers, right? I really try to be easy to work with, I promise. I just... I was just so focused on doing everything perfectly that I guess I took things a little too personally. That's understandable when you're under pressure, right?
Before this most recent nine-month period of feeling down and exhausted, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or hopeless for several weeks or more?

Um... well... before these last nine months? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to be a pretty positive person, you know? 

I guess... I mean, everyone has bad days where they feel a little sad or tired, right? That's just normal life. But feeling hopeless for weeks at a time? No, I really don't think I've ever dealt with anything like that before. I've always tried to just keep my chin up and keep working hard. 

I really try not to let myself get too down, because I know people depend on me to be cheerful and helpful at work. It's important to keep a good attitude, isn't it? I hope I'm answering that right... I just really don't remember ever feeling this exhausted and down before all this started.
Before this current period of feeling down and exhausted, have you ever had a time where you felt so depressed that it interfered with your daily life for more than just a few days?

Um... no, like I was saying, I really don't think so. I mean, before these last nine months, I was always pretty good at just pushing through whatever was going on. 

I definitely wouldn't say I ever felt depressed enough that it stopped me from doing what I needed to do. I've always been really reliable, especially at work. I know how important it is to show up and do a good job, you know? Even if I felt a little tired or stressed, I would never let it interfere with my daily life like that. 

I mean, that's what a responsible person does, right? You just keep going. I really try to be the kind of person who doesn't let things get to them too much. So, yeah, this whole feeling down thing is really new for me. I hope that makes sense? I just... I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a distinct period of unusually elevated (confident) or irritable mood, which directly corresponds to the Elevated_Irritable_Mood symptom.

patient.answer:
Um... well... I guess my mood was a little bit all over the place, if I'm being completely honest. I mean, mostly I just felt... amazing. Like, really, really good and capable, like I could handle anything they threw at me. 

But... um... there were a few times where I guess I wasn't as polite as I should have been. Like, if one of the nurses corrected my documentation, or... or if they told me I needed to slow down and stop doing so much. I... I kind of snapped at them. 

I feel really bad about it now. At the time, it just felt like they were insulting me, or telling me I wasn't doing a good job when I was trying so hard. I know I shouldn't have reacted that way. It's not professional to get irritable with your coworkers, right? I really try to be easy to work with, I promise. I just... I was just so focused on doing everything perfectly that I guess I took things a little too personally. That's understandable when you're under pressure, right?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had any other major depressive episodes in the past, as this would support a diagnosis of F33.3 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, Current Episode Severe) over F31.3 (Bipolar I Disorder, Current Episode Depressed).
doctor.question: Before this most recent nine-month period of feeling down and exhausted, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or hopeless for several weeks or more?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about prior episodes of depression before the current 9-month period, which is not mentioned in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um... well... before these last nine months? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to be a pretty positive person, you know? 

I guess... I mean, everyone has bad days where they feel a little sad or tired, right? That's just normal life. But feeling hopeless for weeks at a time? No, I really don't think I've ever dealt with anything like that before. I've always tried to just keep my chin up and keep working hard. 

I really try not to let myself get too down, because I know people depend on me to be cheerful and helpful at work. It's important to keep a good attitude, isn't it? I hope I'm answering that right... I just really don't remember ever feeling this exhausted and down before all this started.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced any other major depressive episodes prior to the current one, which would support a diagnosis of Recurrent Major Depressive Disorder (F33.3) over Bipolar I Disorder (F31.3).
doctor.question: Before this current period of feeling down and exhausted, have you ever had a time where you felt so depressed that it interfered with your daily life for more than just a few days?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of depressive episodes prior to the current one. The patient's profile only covers the current 9-month depressive episode, and they already answered in the previous turn that they have no prior history.

patient.answer:
Um... no, like I was saying, I really don't think so. I mean, before these last nine months, I was always pretty good at just pushing through whatever was going on. 

I definitely wouldn't say I ever felt depressed enough that it stopped me from doing what I needed to do. I've always been really reliable, especially at work. I know how important it is to show up and do a good job, you know? Even if I felt a little tired or stressed, I would never let it interfere with my daily life like that. 

I mean, that's what a responsible person does, right? You just keep going. I really try to be the kind of person who doesn't let things get to them too much. So, yeah, this whole feeling down thing is really new for me. I hope that makes sense? I just... I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presented with a distinct manic episode followed by a major depressive episode, fulfilling criteria for bipolar I disorder, currently in a depressed phase. The manic episode included elevated mood, increased goal-directed activity, decreased need for sleep, and irritability, lasting for two months. The subsequent depressive episode has lasted over nine months, with persistent low energy, feelings of hopelessness, and functional impairment.
